- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of forecast horizon).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, failing to account for sharp downward corrections after spikes.
- Model underreacts to recent low prices; fails to adjust downward when history shows mean reversion toward lower levels.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ → 85+), then fails to correct downward quickly.
- Forecasts lag behind true price movements, particularly in the 10–20 day range.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 30-day forecast, especially when recent history includes volatility or sharp drops.
- When true outcome shows a strong downward trend, model continues to project upward slope, ignoring recent data.
- Model fails to capture sudden reversals or “rebound” patterns after sharp declines.
- Forecasts are overly smooth; fail to reflect volatility or sudden jumps in true price data.
- Model overconfident in linear extrapolation; ignores non-linear corrections or mean-reversion behavior.
